title: Adaptive call-continuation adapter for hierarchical tool names
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Problem: OpenAI-style tool descriptors (name + schema) and our legacy function metadata have diverged along three axes: hierarchical names (module.sub.name), partial/optional parameter sets, and streaming/continuation semantics. This results in failures when hosted customers migrate from legacy function calls to the OpenAI tool-style surface or when requests cross runtime boundaries (hosted -> dedicated -> private).

Goal: Implement an adapter layer in the runtime that can: (1) resolve hierarchical tool names with configurable aliasing, (2) perform progressive signature marshalling that accepts subset/extra params and applies safe defaults or coercions, and (3) stitch streaming continuations across runtime-shim boundaries so that chunked responses and subsequent calls maintain provenance and KV-cache consistency. The adapter should be gradual (opt-in per-route), observable, and reversible to support canary rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: Adapter resolves hierarchical names with an alias table and fuzzy-matching flag; unit tests cover module.sub/name, module-sub-name, and legacy flat names

Runtime correctly marshals a tool call when client provides a partial argset: missing args are filled using route defaults or verified fallbacks; extra args are dropped or stored in metadata based on policy
Streaming boundaries are preserved: a model that begins a stream via the adapter writes a continuation token that the adapter can rehydrate across hosted/dedicated/private handoffs
Canary rollout via per-route config works: observable metrics show success rate, latency delta, and failure classifications; rollback toggle tested
No regressions for legacy function calls: existing end-to-end tests for legacy function surface pass unchanged
comments: 2025-02-15 Diego: Spike complete. Prototype resolves hierarchical names by splitting on both '.' and '/' and then attempts longest-prefix matching against the alias registry. Found edge-case where names differ only by casing; patched registry to be case-insensitive by default.

2025-02-18 Priya: Design review notes — prefer explicit alias table managed in Console instead of purely heuristic fuzzy-matching. Add audit log entries for ambiguous resolves. Also prefer policy-driven handling of extra params: 'reject' | 'drop' | 'attach-metadata'.
2025-02-22 Maya Chen (Design): UX for per-route toggle looks good. Suggest exposing a preview mode that shows how a given historical call would be transformed by the adapter (non-destructive).

2025-02-25 Diego: Implemented progressive marshalling. Strategy: use param-level validators and coercers defined in schema. If value missing and route default exists, fill and annotate the call metadata. If coercion occurs, include telemetry tag 'coercion=type'.

2025-02-28 QA: Found a race where streaming rehydration fails when adapter state is persisted and immediately evicted; root cause: continuation token included ephemeral runtime instance id. Workaround in adapter: persist only logical token (model, request-id, seq) and let runtime rebind instance arn during rehydrate.

2025-03-02 Diego: Added telemetry counters and tracing spans for resolve path, marshalling decisions, and continuation rehydrates. Sending a small set of events to Console observability backend for the canary route.

2025-03-04 Security: quick review - no secrets are stored in adapter tokens. Recommend KMS signing for continuation tokens to avoid tampering across private deployments. Marking security_review_required=true if we enable cross-customer token exchange.

2025-03-05 Priya: Preparing rollout plan: start internal canary (redwood-internal) for 48 hours, then invite three pilot customers with dedicated capacity. Will monitor success_rate, avg_latency_delta, and 'resolve_ambiguous' per 1k calls.
